motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the consent agenda. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion. The motion passed with a unanimous vote.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: Everything grouped on the consent agenda passed in a single vote, with the record here not listing the individual items it held.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain Citg, Utah, Amending the Parkwag Fields (Ault Farms) Master Development Agreement (MDA)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wr@ht moved to approve an ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending the Parkway Fields Master Development Plan as presented. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion. The motion passed with a unanimous vote.
motions.headline: Parkway Fields phases and layout redrawn
motions.summary: The council approved a redrawn Parkway Fields plan that splits the townhome phase in two and adds about four townhomes, offset by fewer lots in a later phase.
motions.impact: The number of homes on the site does not go up. If you are buying there, phase and plat labels changed, and the developer told the council it will dedicate land along Old Airport Road for a trail and trailhead.

motions.summary: The council updated the master development agreement behind Parkway Fields, the Ault Farms project, so the contract matches the site's revised plan.
motions.impact: This is the contract that fixes what the builder owes the city there. Buyers and neighbors in Parkway Fields are the ones it reaches; the rest of the city will not notice.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 17.10.030 Definitions, 16.50.020 Purpose, 16.50.030 Application and 16.50.040 Approval Process Mayor Westmoreland opened the public hearing at lO:16 p.m. As there were no comments, he closed the hearing. Discussion ensued regarding whether information about existing property entitlements, specifically animal rights or buffering, needed to be added to the standards; concerns with land use conflicts; and factors requiring the approval or denial of a lot line adjustment. Mr. Draper stated that language could be added to the standards recognizing that a lot may have multiple zones and that a lot line adjustment does not alter zoning. He clarified that applications would need to comply with the terms of an applicable MDA and land use ordinances. Mr. Larsen noted that this amendment is specific to lot line adjustments rather than uses. When a property has two zones, generally land use code includes a provision that the most restrictive requirement prevails. motions.headline: Fence and buffer rules rewritten
motions.summary: The city rewrote its fencing rules, declaring broken, flammable or spite fences unlawful nuisances, adding a split-rail definition, and barring berms or hedges where a wall is required.
motions.impact: A fence that is falling apart, or one put up to needle a neighbor, can now be treated as a nuisance and ordered fixed. Staff will bring back separate changes on commercial buffers and fences where the ground drops away.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.08, Form of Government and Section 2.15.120 Presiding Officer with the following amendments: l. EMMC 2.18.080, "No new city policies, code, ordinance, or resolution shall be created and enacted by mayor or staff without the consent of the majority vote of city council In an open and public meeting; and 2. EMMC 2.15.120(B), "Discuss and make all assignments to each city council member and the mayor that promote and enhance necessary representation and support for the citizens of the city. The mayor will make a recommendation of liaison assignments, the council will then discuss the assignments and vote on the final assignments. lt will pass with a majority vote." AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.08, Form of Government and Section 2.15.120 Presiding Officer with the following amendments: l. EMMC 2.18.080, "No new city policies, code, ordinance, or resolution shall be created and enacted by mayor or staff without the consent of the majority vote of city council In an open and public meeting; 2. EMMC 2.15.120(B), "Discuss and make all assignments to each city council member and the mayor that promote and enhance necessary representation and support for the citizens of the city. The mayor will make a recommendation of liaison assignments, the council will then discuss the assignments and vote on the final assignments. lt will pass with a majority vote;" and 3. EMMC 2.08.030, one one member of the six-member council shall make decisions for the body nor shall any member of the body knowingly give the perception to an organization, or Individual citizen, or staff that they are authorized to represent the full body without the city council's vote and approval In an open and public meetin1." Councilmember Gray seconded the motion. Discussion clarified that the standards will only apply to liaison assignments and not the mauor's committee assignments and that the mayor could function as a liaison in the place of a councilmember. The motion passed with a unanimous vote.
motions.headline: Council limits mayor's power to set policy
motions.summary: The council wrote into code that neither the mayor nor staff may enact city policy without a majority council vote, and that no member may speak for the full body.
motions.impact: City policy now has to clear a public council vote before it takes effect, so more of it happens in front of you at a meeting. Liaison assignments also go to a council vote rather than the mayor alone.

motions.headline: 2024 board liaison assignments set
motions.summary: The council handed each member board assignments for the year, from the cemetery and arts boards to the Planning Commission and the Utah League of Cities and Towns.
motions.impact: If you sit on one of those boards, you now know which councilmember will be in the room with you. For everyone else this is an internal calendar.
